blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Time in business English is short and clear. In a London office, people say the time many times a day. "At 9 am," "at half past two," "quarter to five" — these are very common.

We use "at" before a clock time. The market opens at nine. Our meeting is at half past two. Lunch is at one o'clock. The office closes at six.

"Half past 2" means 2:30. "Quarter to 5" means 4:45. "Quarter past 9" means 9:15. For a call, always say London time. Being on time is a sign of respect.

items.q: What word do we use before a clock time?
items.why: "We use 'at' before a clock time." — at nine, at six.

items.q: What time does the office close?
items.why: "The office closes at six."

items.q: What does "quarter to five" mean?
items.why: "Quarter to 5" = 4:45 (falta um quarto de hora para as 5).

items.q: The text says to always say London time for a call. This suggests that…
options: the people are in different time zones
items.why: Inferência: só dizemos o fuso (London time) quando as pessoas estão em lugares diferentes.

items.q: The author would most likely AGREE that…
options: it is fine to arrive late
you should never say the time
items.why: Inferência: "Being on time is a sign of respect." — o texto valoriza a pontualidade.

blocks.instruction: Ouça o colega explicando os horários. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Hi! Let me help you with the meeting time. In London, we say time in a simple way, but you need to listen well.

Our team meeting is at half past two. So it starts at two thirty, not two o'clock. Please be there five minutes early. Being on time is very important here.

The market opens at nine in the morning, and it is very busy then. Lunch is at one o'clock, so we have a small break. The office closes at six in the evening.

If we have a call with New York, I always say London time. New York is behind us, so we must be clear. Nine here is not nine there.

One more thing: "quarter to five" means four forty-five. "Quarter past nine" means nine fifteen. It is easy when you practise. See you at the meeting!
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What time does the team meeting start?
items.why: "Our team meeting is at half past two. So it starts at two thirty."

items.q: What time does the market open?
items.why: "The market opens at nine in the morning."

items.q: Why does the speaker say "be there five minutes early"?
options: Because being on time is important
items.why: Inferência: ele liga chegar cedo a "Being on time is very important here."

items.q: Why does the speaker always say "London time" for a call with New York?
options: Because the two cities have different times
items.why: Inferência: "New York is behind us" — os fusos são diferentes, então ele deixa claro.

items.q: What does "quarter past nine" mean?
items.why: "'Quarter past nine' means nine fifteen." (9:15).

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "The train leaves at three o'clock." O'clock means…
items.why: O'clock = em ponto, na hora exata (3:00).

items.q: Choose the correct word: "The class is at ___ past two, so it starts at 2:30."
items.why: Half past = e meia. Half past two = 2:30.

items.q: "It is a quarter to five." A quarter is…
items.why: Quarter = quarto de hora = 15 minutos. Quarter to five = 4:45.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "The market opens at nine in the ___."
items.why: Morning = manhã. Nine in the morning = 9 da manhã.

items.q: "We finish at six in the evening." Evening means…
items.why: Evening = fim de tarde / noite (cedo).

blocks.instruction: Expressões simples de trabalho com horários e reuniões. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "Let's set up a meeting for ten o'clock." To set up means to…
items.why: Set up = marcar, organizar (uma reunião).

items.q: "Please be on time for the call." To be on time means to…
items.why: Be on time = chegar na hora certa, ser pontual.

items.q: "Can we put off the meeting to three o'clock?" To put off means to…
items.why: Put off = adiar, deixar para depois.

items.q: "The market opens up at nine." To open up means to…
items.why: Open up = abrir, começar a funcionar.

items.q: "I need to check in before the meeting starts." To check in means to…
options: report or confirm you are there
items.why: Check in = dar um retorno, confirmar presença/status.
